relationships.subject: rACC-VTA glutamatergic projection neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Pharmacogenetic inhibition of glutamatergic neurons of rACC projecting to the VTA alleviated the CPA responses and itch-scratching behavior induced by the subcutaneous injection of 5-HT, a nonhistamine-dependent pruritogen.

relationships.subject: rACC neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: pharmacogenetic inhibition of rACC neurons did not change the CPA behavior associated with itch and, conversely, increased itch-scratching behavior

key_findings: Inhibiting rACC-to-VTA glutamatergic neurons reduced 5-HT-induced CPA and scratching in rats.
Global rACC inhibition increased scratching without changing itch CPA.
